sn46.5:1.2: Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One … and said to him:
sn46.5:1.5: In what sense are they called factors of enlightenment?” “They lead to enlightenment, bhikkhu, therefore they are called factors of enlightenment.
sn46.5:1.6: Here, bhikkhu, one develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness,
sn46.5:1.7: which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release…. One develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release.
sn46.5:1.8: While one is developing these seven factors of enlightenment, one’s mind is liberated from the taint of sensuality, from the taint of existence, from the taint of ignorance.
sn46.5:1.9: When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated.’
sn46.5:1.10: One understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’
sn46.5:1.11: They lead to enlightenment, bhikkhu, therefore they are called factors of enlightenment.”
